text.p: Italian debt markets started firmer in line with many other European bond markets which were all attempting to consolidate after recent losses, dealers said.

Despite the overnight slide in T-bonds, BTPs chose to follow the firmer trend to other bond markets such as bunds and take support from the confirmation of Italy's July CPI annual rate of 1.6 percent after 1.4 percent in June.
Dealers said the markets were unruffled by move by the Bundesbank today to set a 14-day repo tender at fixed rate of 3.0 percent, and make no immediate comment on any other money market activities.
Despite the CPI figures, dealers say the market is still concerned over the high value of dollar against the lira, and the potential effect this may have on Italian inflation.
However, in early trading BTP futures began to push ahead and the September LIFFE contract showed gains of 30 basis point to 136.20 by 0745 GMT.
"The BTPs underperformed bunds yesterday, so there was some catching up to do today," said one LIFFE dealer.
